'''Ise Calendar''' (伊勢暦) refers to the {{ill|Calendar|en|Calendar|qid=Q12132|lt=calendar}} produced and distributed by {{ill|calendar makers|ja|暦師|qid=Q140446111}} in {{ill|Uji (disambiguation)|ceb|Uji|de|Uji|eo|UJI|es|Uji|fr|Uji (homonymie)|it|UJI|ja|宇治|pl|Uji|ru|Удзи (значения)|sv|Uji|qid=Q422616|lt=Uji (Ise)}} and {{ill|Yamada (disambiguation)|be|Ямада|ceb|Yamada|de|Yamada|fa|یامادا|fr|Yamada|it|Yamada|ja|山田|ko|야마다|nl|Yamada|ru|Ямада|sv|Yamada|uk|Ямада|zh|山田|qid=Q355196|lt=Yamada (Ise)}}, located in front of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise Grand Shrine}} during the {{ill|Edo period|en|Edo period|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}}. It is the predecessor of today’s {{ill|Jingū calendar|fr|Calendriers Jingū|ja|神宮暦|qid=Q11589491|lt=Jingū calendar}}.

== Overview ==

The Ise Calendar became known throughout Japan as {{ill|Onshi|ja|御師|qid=Q11488972}} from Ise distributed it along with {{ill|Jingū taima|ja|神宮大麻|simple|Jingū taima|zh|神宮大麻|qid=Q11589469|lt=Jingū Taima}} (sacred talismans from Ise Grand Shrine) at the end of the year. There were around 14 to 20 calendar makers in Yamada ({{ill|Toyōke Daijingū|ja|外宮|lt=Gekū (Outer Shrine)}}) depending on the period, and one calendar maker in Uji ({{ill|Kōtai Jingū|ja|内宮|zh|內宮|qid=Q23996212|lt=Naikū (Inner Shrine)}}).

In {{ill|1871|en|1871|qid=Q7746|lt=1871}} ({{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}} 4), the Onshi system was abolished, and the distribution of the Ise Calendar was also discontinued. In April {{ill|1882|en|1882|qid=Q7812|lt=1882}}, a proclamation from the {{ill|Daijō-kan|en|Daijō-kan|qid=Q1192939|lt=Daijō-kan}} decreed that from {{ill|1883|en|1883|qid=Q7816|lt=1883}} (Meiji 16), official calendars would be issued by the {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|ja|神宮司庁|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 伊勢神宮|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q687168}}, and thus the publication of the calendar continued under the name "Jingū Calendar."
